---
title: "Project documentation"
---

Fit statistical models directly in PHP using ordinary numeric arrays. The native
Rust engine returns coefficients, uncertainty, fitted values, and model statistics.
A fixed intercept is added automatically; `intercept: false` accepts a literal
design or fits a model through the origin.

```php
$result = Phit\fit_ols(
    x: [[74.4], [57.4], [66.4], [49.1], [45.7], [92.4], [37.0], [93.9]],
    y: [1879.25, 1805.03, 2022.29, 1267.85, 1509.24, 2240.10, 959.51, 2386.54],
);
// coefficients: approximately [372.478545, 21.479724] — intercept, floor area.
```

Start with [installation](development.qmd) and the [PHP contracts](contracts.qmd).
For unequal exposure in a Poisson model, pass `offset: log(exposure)` as an aligned
array on the log scale; see the [exposure example](contracts.qmd#poisson-exposure-example).
Existing callers that supply a ones column should remove it or use
`intercept: false`; random-effect design matrices remain explicit.

The [math walkthroughs](notebooks/index.qmd) build the matrices and likelihoods
step by step. The verification pages compare the same models with R, Python,
and independent numerical references.

Keep the root README as a quick entry point. Put detailed guidance here and
update the relevant document alongside code changes. Distinguish implemented
behavior, verified behavior and proposed direction; do not present plans as
existing features. Add new documents only when a topic needs its own explanation.
